subject: government
topic: Nationalism and constitutional development to independence

kept.q: Which notable Nigerian nationalist founded the West African Pilot newspaper, which was widely used to campaign against colonial rule and spread nationalist ideas among Nigerians?
kept.explanation: Nnamdi Azikiwe founded the West African Pilot in 1937 and used it to criticise colonial rule and awaken nationalist consciousness in Nigerians.
kept.pidgin: Na Nnamdi Azikiwe start West African Pilot for 1937, e dey use am criticize colonial government and wake up nationalist feeling for Nigerians.

kept.q: Which Nigerian constitution, introduced in 1922, first allowed a small number of educated Nigerians in Lagos and Calabar to elect their own representatives into the Legislative Council?
kept.explanation: The 1922 Clifford Constitution introduced the elective principle, allowing Lagos and Calabar to elect a few members into the Legislative Council for the first time.
kept.pidgin: Na Clifford Constitution of 1922 bring elective principle, wey make Lagos and Calabar fit elect small members enter Legislative Council for the first time.

kept.q: Which constitution, introduced in 1946, first divided Nigeria into three regions (Northern, Eastern and Western) and created regional houses of assembly?
kept.explanation: The Richards Constitution of 1946 divided Nigeria into three regions and set up regional houses, laying the foundation for the federal system Nigeria later adopted.
kept.pidgin: Na Richards Constitution of 1946 first divide Nigeria into three regions and bring regional houses, na im start the federal arrangement Nigeria later take.

kept.q: A key feature of the 1954 Lyttleton Constitution was that it...
options: merged the three regions into a single unitary state
introduced a strong federal system with each region enjoying self-government in internal affairs
kept.explanation: The Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 firmly established federalism, granting each region control over its own internal affairs while a central government handled common national matters.
kept.pidgin: Lyttleton Constitution of 1954 bring strong federal system, where every region fit control dia own internal matter while central government dey handle common national issues.

kept.q: The Action Group (AG), led by Chief Obafemi Awolowo, drew its strongest political support mainly from which group of Nigerians?
kept.explanation: The Action Group was formed in 1951 mainly to champion the political and cultural interests of the Yoruba-speaking people of Western Nigeria.
kept.pidgin: Action Group, wey Awolowo lead, get im main support from Yoruba people for Western Nigeria.

kept.q: In 1953, Chief Anthony Enahoro moved a motion in the House of Representatives calling for Nigeria's self-government by 1956. Opposition to this motion by which party led to a walkout and eventually sparked riots in Kano?
options: National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC)
kept.explanation: Northern leaders in the NPC felt the North was not yet ready for self-government by 1956, so they opposed the motion and walked out of the House, a disagreement that later led to the 1953 Kano riots.
kept.pidgin: Northern leaders for NPC no gree with the 1956 self-government motion, dem argue say North never ready, dem waka comot for House, and the tension later cause Kano riot for 1953.

kept.q: Which of the following was NOT a major factor that encouraged the rise of nationalism in colonial Nigeria?
options: Impact of the Second World War on colonial subjects
Formation of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS)
kept.explanation: ECOWAS was formed in 1975, well after Nigeria gained independence in 1960, so it could not have caused the earlier nationalist agitation; the other options were genuine pre-independence influences.
kept.pidgin: ECOWAS start for 1975, afta Nigeria don independent since 1960, so e no fit be one of the things wey cause nationalism before independence; the other options na real factors wey cause am.

kept.q: The National Council of Nigeria and the Cameroons (NCNC), founded in 1944, was initially formed mainly to...
options: organize the first military coup in Nigeria
unite Nigerians and Cameroonians in the struggle for better political and economic conditions
oversee local government elections in Lagos
kept.explanation: The NCNC was founded in 1944 as a pressure group to unite Nigerians and Cameroonians under British rule to press for political and economic reforms and later self-government.
kept.pidgin: Dem form NCNC for 1944 as pressure group make Nigerians and Cameroonians unite fight together for better political and economic condition, and later self-government.
